b1: The Fastest-Growing Train Routes in Europe for 2026
b2: By WoW Train · August 2026 · 7 min read
b3: Rail travel across Europe isn't just holding steady this year — it's surging. Bookings on some routes have jumped by 40-50% compared to last year, new sleeper trains are relaunching connections that disappeared decades ago, and a whole generation of travelers is choosing the train as part of the trip, not just a way to get there. Here's what's actually driving the numbers, and which routes are worth booking now.
b4: Why train travel is having a moment
b5: A few forces are pushing this at once. "Flygskam" — flight shame — has gone from a Swedish niche concept to a mainstream reason people choose rail over short-haul flights, especially for journeys under six hours. The EU's climate targets are pushing real investment into cross-border rail infrastructure. And socially, sleeper cabins and sunrise views from dining cars have become their own kind of travel content — the train isn't just transport anymore, it's part of the story people want to tell about the trip.
b7: Bookings up more than 50% year over year
b8: This is the standout number of the season. Two of Central Europe's most atmospheric capitals, connected by a comfortable EuroCity service through the Slovak countryside — no wonder it's become one of the fastest-growing routes on the continent. Both cities reward a few days each: Budapest's thermal baths and ruin bars, Prague's old town and castle district.
b10: Bookings up around 45% year over year
b11: A short, frequent, high-speed hop between two of Europe's most walkable capitals — canals and museums in Amsterdam, medieval squares and comic-strip murals in Brussels. It's an easy add-on to almost any Northern Europe itinerary, and the growth here reflects how many travelers are stacking two or three cities into a single week rather than picking just one.
b13: A faster daytime connection between Paris and Munich launched this year, cutting a route that used to feel like an afterthought into a genuine one-day option — French elegance to Bavarian beer halls and Alpine views, no flight required.
b15: A new daytime link now stitches together Central Europe and Scandinavia in a single journey — Prague's spires to Copenhagen's harbourfront, a combination that used to require a flight or an awkward multi-train relay.
b17: A couple of 2026 launches haven't made it into our booking tool yet, but they're worth knowing about if you're planning ahead. A new night train now links Basel and Malmö, threading Switzerland to southern Sweden in a single overnight hop — one of the clearest signs of the sleeper-train revival in action. And a new service connects London and Stirling in Scotland, opening up the Highlands gateway without a domestic flight. We'll add both as soon as ticketing support is live.
